title: AMD Jumps 7% as Semiconductor Rebound Reaches a Third Session; Broadcom Rises 3%, NVIDIA Edges Higher
excerpt: Semiconductor stocks are posting a third straight session of gains, but one chip name is running so far ahead of the pack that it raises an uncomfortable que...
content_html:
Quick Read

  • AMD surged 7% to lead chips for a third straight session, with Broadcom up 3% and NVIDIA gaining 2% on sector momentum alone.

  • SOXX jumped 3% while QQQ rose just 2%, confirming today's strength is concentrated in semiconductors rather than broad large-cap tech.

  • AMD is up 156% year-to-date versus Broadcom's 1%, making it the highest-beta chip play that can reverse fast on any weak session.

  • Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and NVIDIA didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat NVDA. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) is leading a third consecutive session of gains for semiconductor stocks, with AMD stock up 7% to $548.76 in Thursday afternoon trading. The move sits inside a broad chip bounce, with the iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) up 3% to $519.50. AMD stock is running well ahead of the sector benchmark that holds it.

The wider NASDAQ 100 tape is quieter today. The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is up 2% to $716.41, so the day's strength is concentrated in chips rather than large-cap tech more broadly. That backdrop matters, because the AMD move is a group story rather than a solo one.

Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) stock is up 3% to $349.02, extending prior gains tied to AI accelerator momentum. Also rising, NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) stock is up 2% to $218.70, edging higher as the group's market-cap leader while AMD carries the larger percentage gain of the three.

Sector Rebound, Not a Company Event

Today's action in AMD reflects a semiconductor rebound reaching its third consecutive session rather than an earnings release, guidance change or analyst rating action, and AMD stock is the highest-beta way to own that bounce inside the large-cap chip group.

One same-day development at AMD is worth naming, and it explicitly isn't the catalyst here. Advanced Micro Devices said it is working with SiFive to tune its open-source ROCm software so it runs on RISC-V datacenter servers for AI workloads. No reporting connects that announcement to the size of the price move, so the article treats it as strategy rather than trigger.
